newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU to send Ireland's Spring on Middle East mission.
newsitem.headline: EU to send Ireland's Spring on Middle East mission.

text.p: The European Union, frustrated by by being left out of U.S.-brokered Middle East peace moves, decided on Saturday to send Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring to the region to meet both Palestinians and Israelis.
Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said Spring would go to the Middle East "at the earliest possible time in the coming week".
Bruton said European Union leaders meeting in Dublin also agreed to appoint a special envoy to try to help rebuild the Middle East peace process, shaken by renewed violence.
The precise role to be performed by the envoy would have to be worked out later, but it was to focus mainly on economic issues.
Spring, meanwhile, was to take a letter to both Israel and the Palestinian Authority expressing the EU's desire to help in any way possible.
Bruton said Spring would "convey the strongly-held views of all member countries of the European Union of the need to accelerate the peace process."
The EU has been frustrated at its exclusion from U.S. Middle East peace moves, particularly since it is by far the largest donor of humanitarian and development aid in support of the peace process.
British Prime Minister John Major said: "We can apply pressure but it is the Israelis and Palestinians alone which will determine whether progress is made or not."
French President Jacques Chirac said the EU's approach was to be even handed.
"It's not a question for the EU to be for one or for the other," he told reporters. "It is for peace."
A spokesman for Spring said he would leave as soon as possible but no time had been agreed yet.
